_note: Public safety records (satsang-extensions 19 under the Satsang publication rule). Dry, attributed, dated; each with its primary reports.

records.subject: person/yogi-bhajan
records.summary: After December 2019 allegations (incl. Dyson's memoir), Yogi Bhajan's own organization commissioned An Olive Branch. Interviewing 299 people, the August 2020 report found it more likely than not that he engaged in sexual battery, sexual abuse, harassment and unethical conduct with 36 followers (1969–2004), with organizational enablers named. SSSC published it unedited.

reports.outlet: SSSC letter publishing the An Olive Branch report
Yoga Journal: A New Report Details Decades of Abuse

records.subject: person/taizan-maezumi
records.summary: Maezumi admitted alcoholism and sexual relationships with students in 1983 (Betty Ford rehab); his own organization later published findings, reforms and an ongoing atonement process.

reports.outlet: Tricycle: American Zen Community in Crisis (Cushman)

records.subject: person/sogyal-rinpoche
records.summary: After a July 2017 letter from eight former students, Rigpa commissioned an independent investigation (Lewis Silkin, led by Karen Baxter). The August 2018 report found, on the balance of probabilities, that some inner-circle students were subjected to serious physical, sexual and emotional abuse, and that senior Rigpa figures knew of some issues and failed to act. Not all allegations were upheld. Rigpa published the report and its boards' response.

reports.outlet: UK Charity Commission inquiry: Rigpa Fellowship

records.subject: place/school-of-philosophy-london
records.summary: St James and St Vedast schools in London were founded in 1975 by members of the School of Economic Science (SES). An independent inquiry commissioned in 2005 by the schools' owners and chaired by James Townend QC found that pupils had been "criminally assaulted" and suffered mental and physical mistreatment. The schools apologised unreservedly; by December 2020 about £1m had been paid to 45 former pupils in settlements without admission of liability (BBC). The record concerns the schools, not the SES's current adult classes.

reports.outlet: BBC News: Pupils' historical abuse at London schools claims total £1m
TES: Inquiry reveals culture of violence

records.subject: place/iyi-new-york
records.summary: In November 2023 two former students sued Integral Yoga Institute, Inc. and Satchidananda Ashram-Yogaville, Inc. under New York's Adult Survivors Act, alleging that founder Swami Satchidananda (d. 2002) sexually abused them as teenagers in the late 1960s and that the Institute failed to investigate. On 15 January 2026 the Appellate Division (S.N. v Integral Yoga Inst., 2026 NY Slip Op 00217) upheld dismissal of the organisations' counterclaims as SLAPP claims; the abuse claims themselves have not been decided. Former disciples first raised allegations publicly in 1991; Satchidananda denied them.

reports.outlet: S.N. v Integral Yoga Inst., Inc., 2026 NY Slip Op 00217 (App Div 1st Dept)
The New Yorker: Yoga reconsiders the role of the guru in the age of #MeToo

records.subject: person/swami-vishnudevananda
records.summary: In December 2019 Julie Salter, his former personal assistant, publicly alleged that Swami Vishnudevananda (founder of the International Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres, d. 1993) sexually abused her for over three years at the Canadian headquarters; other women made similar allegations. The BBC (2021) interviewed 14 women alleging abuse by senior Sivananda teachers. The organisation's board apologised for historic mistakes in handling the allegations and commissioned an independent investigation; a community-funded investigation (Project SATYA) published interim reports in 2020.

reports.outlet: BBC News: 'Coercion and rape': Investigating my yoga school (Ishleen Kaur)
Project SATYA Interim Report #3 (Carol Merchasin), allegations against Swami Vishnudevananda

records.subject: person/swami-rama
records.summary: On 4 September 1997 a US federal jury (M.D. Pa., Patel v. Himalayan International Institute) awarded US$275,000 compensatory and US$1.6 million punitive damages against the Himalayan Institute, finding that its founder Swami Rama had sexual relations with a 19-year-old student by abusing his position as her guru, and that the Institute was negligent in allowing him to be a sexual predator for years. The court upheld the verdict in December 1999. Yoga Journal had reported allegations by several women in 1990.

reports.outlet: Patel v. Himalayan International Institute, 3:CV-94-1118 (M.D. Pa. 9 Dec 1999), memorandum
Yoga Journal: The Case against Swami Rama of the Himalayas (Katharine Webster), Dec 1990 (reprint)
